emily: Heads up — I ran an invoice-preview job and the prefetch/cache credits looked off. Prefetch hits are getting applied to the responder route, so previews show >100% cache savings for some customers. Anyone seen this?

sam: Yep. Our current crediting is simple: credit the route that served the cached response (fast to compute). Prefetch origin info isn't currently used for attribution.

julia: I pulled a small sample. Example: routeA triggers prefetch for model-x, prefetch_id=pf_abc. Later routeB hits the cache and shows a hit. Invoice preview credited routeB with the savings even though routeA paid the prefetch token cost. Numbers: prefetch tokens=1.8k, observed credited savings=2.1k (double counts in some windows).

mike: That was intentional tradeoff originally — easier runtime and avoids tracking lineage. But for invoice previews / actual chargeback we need deterministic allocation. Options: 1) attribute to triggering route (sticky mapping), 2) amortize savings across beneficiaries, 3) leave as-is and add explanatory note in UI.

emily: My preference is (2) amortize in preview but keep runtime cheap. Proposal: when prefetch writes KV, tag the entry with `prefetch_id` + `origin_route`. In billing pipeline, join cache-hit events on `prefetch_id` within a TTL window and amortize the prefetch cost across unique beneficiary routes. That avoids retroactive double-crediting.

julia: Sounds good. For sampled invoice runs we should be careful: sampling variance will make amortization look noisy. Suggest deterministic hashing for amortization buckets so preview is stable across runs.

sam: Implementation note: runtime already exposes `prefetch_id` on the KV envelope in logs. We need to surface that in our batch ETL and add an index on `prefetch_id`. Minimal proto change: add optional string prefetch_origin and required string prefetch_id when prefetch occurs. Example proto snippet:
```proto
message PrefetchMeta {
  string prefetch_id = 1;
  string origin_route = 2; // e.g. /routes/routeA
}
message KVEnvelope {
  bytes key = 1;
  bytes value = 2;
  PrefetchMeta prefetch = 10; // nullable
}
```

mike: Ops concern: tracking `prefetch_id` at scale for 7d could blow up storage/indexes. For previews we can TTL lineage to 24h and run preview jobs only on that window. Also consider Bloom filter per-prefetch to track unique beneficiaries instead of full lists.

emily: Agree TTL 24h is fine for preview fidelity. For true billing we need a different path (contracted Dedicated customers). Let's keep previews conservative.

julia: For amortization math: allocate prefetch_token_cost / unique_beneficiaries. Use deterministic beneficiary set by de-duplicating route+tenant in the window. If we use hashing we can show confidence bands in UI.

sam: I can add prefetch_id wiring in the ETL and a small map-reduce job to compute per-prefetch beneficiary counts. Will need an index on event(prefetch_id).

mike: If we go heavy on indices, let's run a cap test on staging with 24h TTL and 5M prefetch events/day. I'll allocate cluster.

billing-bot: Billing preview run #2245 finished — processed 12,344 previews, flagged 87 prefetch anomalies. Report: https://console.internal/reports/2245

emily: Thanks — I'll draft the UX copy: "Invoice preview shows amortized prefetch credits across routes that benefited within 24h; actual billing for Dedicated customers may differ." cc @julia to validate wording.

julia: I'll run a deterministic-sample and output a diff table (old vs amortized) by EOD.

emily: Cool. Plan: sam -> ETL changes, mike -> staging cap test, julia -> numbers, me -> UX/messaging. Sync tomorrow 10am. Thanks!
